alec-bradley--prensado.description: A box-pressed blend rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, pairing a Honduran wrapper with a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. It smokes with leather, dark chocolate and warm spice, picking up toasted nuts and a dried-fruit depth as the strength gathers; an unhurried cigar for after dinner.

thirds.notes: Toasted almond and wood open the cigar, with a light caramel sweetness and soft spice.
Black pepper moves forward while the nuttiness holds and a darker, dried-fruit note appears.
The smoke turns earthier and drier, with cedar and hazelnut on a finish that gains weight.

sources.title: Big Al's Cigar Blog – Prensado Corona Gorda review
Cigars Lover – Prensado Gran Toro review

alec-bradley--black-market.description: Built around a shipment of Panamanian tobacco and refined over eighteen trial blends, Black Market wraps Panamanian and Honduran filler in a Sumatran binder and a dark Nicaraguan leaf. Pepper and cedar lead, settling over cocoa, coffee and earth with a quiet herbal sweetness behind; steady rather than showy.

thirds.notes: Red and black pepper over earth and cedar, with a soft cocoa sweetness underneath.
The pepper eases; coffee, leather and cedar come forward in a rounder, steadier middle.
Pepper returns with dark chocolate, slightly bitter coffee and toasted oak toward the band.

sources.title: After Action Cigars – Black Market Toro review
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – Black Market

alec-bradley--black-market-esteli.description: An Estelí-focused take on Black Market, with Nicaraguan wrapper and filler and a Nicaraguan-Honduran binder in place of the original's Panamanian leaf. Black pepper, bitter coffee and dark chocolate open over dark fruit; the smoke then turns creamier and nutty before cinnamon, dried fruit and cedar close it out.

thirds.notes: Black pepper sits over bitter coffee and dark chocolate, with a prune-like sweetness beneath.
The spice settles; coffee, a creamy texture and nutty notes carry the middle.
Cinnamon, dried fruit and cedar build with cocoa and leather as the body climbs again.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – Black Market Estelí Torpedo review
Klaro Cigars – Black Market Estelí review

alec-bradley--thirty-years.description: Released for the company's thirtieth year as a 2026 retail exclusive, Thirty Years wraps a Trojes-grown Honduran leaf around a Jamastrán and Jalapa binder, with filler from Estelí, Jalapa, Jamastrán and Trojes. The maker describes savoury leather and toast with a nutty edge, steady pepper and a hint of cinnamon in a medium-full smoke.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Alec Bradley Thirty Years Toro review

thirds.notes: Bread, baking spice and mixed pepper at first, settling into cherry and cedar, with black pepper on the retrohale.
Cherry and cedar hold the centre while pepper slowly climbs and the smoke gains weight.
Pepper becomes the main supporting note behind cherry and cedar, with a faint edge of harshness at the end.

alec-bradley--chunk-sumatra.description: Part of the Chunk series of short, very thick cigars, all four inches long with ring gauges from 60 to 80. An Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper covers an American broadleaf binder and Dominican, Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. Medium in body, it leans on dried fruit, baking spice and cedar; a compact smoke for a relaxed evening outdoors after a hearty meal.

alec-bradley--chunk-maduro.description: The maduro member of the Chunk series: short, four-inch cigars in ring gauges of 60 to 80. A Mexican wrapper encloses a Jamastrán binder from Honduras and filler of Dominican Piloto and Estelí tobacco. Medium in body, it offers a dark molasses sweetness, a steady build of pepper and a warm, nutty finish.

alec-bradley--chunk-shade.description: The mildest of the Chunk cigars, four inches long and 60 to 80 ring gauge, under a pale Honduran Connecticut-seed wrapper with an American broadleaf binder and Dominican, Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. It smokes smooth and light, with sweet, bread-like toast and a gentle hay note from start to finish; suited to a short, easy break.

alec-bradley--do-not-disturb.description: A mellow-to-medium blend made for quiet, uninterrupted time: an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper over a Dominican Criollo binder, with Dominican Piloto and Mexican ligero in the filler. The maker describes steady earth, a soft cedar structure and fresh herbal, grassy notes that keep the smoke light; a calm daytime companion.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Alec Bradley Do Not Disturb (DND) Toro review

thirds.notes: Berry sweetness and cream lead, with cedar arriving early and pepper and chestnut in the background.
Natural tobacco moves up beside the berry note, while cream drops back with the cedar, pepper and chestnut.
Tobacco and berry merge in front; pepper rises a little and the body firms up towards the end.

alec-bradley--safe-keepings.description: A blend recovered from the Alec Bradley founder's blend book and rolled today as a Nicaraguan puro, with Nicaraguan wrapper, binder and filler. Medium to full in body, it opens with warming pepper, builds layered spice through the middle and settles into a subtle cocoa richness at the finish, according to the maker.

alec-bradley--post-embargo-blend-code-b1.description: A newer expression of Post Embargo with a fifth-priming wrapper from Trojes, Honduras, a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. Medium in body, it rests on a mineral, earthy base, with cedar and oak for structure and a lightly toasted nuttiness that adds depth without weight; a measured cigar for an evening drink.

sources.title: Alec Bradley – Post Embargo: Blend Code B15

alec-bradley--double-broadleaf.description: From Alec Bradley's Experimental Series: a Connecticut broadleaf wrapper and binder grown in Honduras, a second binder from Nicaragua, and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Full in body, it is dense and dark, with deep cocoa, a slow molasses sweetness and a steady thread of black pepper; a cigar to keep for after dinner.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Alec Bradley Double Broadleaf Gran Corona review

thirds.notes: Mocha and earth open the smoke, the coffee side of the mocha growing, with red pepper on the retrohale.
The mocha turns into plain coffee beside earth; pepper and cedar strengthen and a touch of citrus appears.
Pepper and cedar join coffee and earth in front, and the profile becomes denser and less distinct.

alec-bradley--kintsugi.description: Named for the Japanese craft of mending pottery with gold, Kintsugi pairs a Trojes-grown Honduran wrapper with a Honduran and Nicaraguan binder and filler. Medium in strength, it opens with cinnamon and white pepper, moves through wood and leather, and finishes on a soft, nougat-like sweetness with a creamy edge.

thirds.notes: White pepper and cinnamon on the retrohale, with a tangy sweetness and a hint of clove.
Richer and woodier, with leather and a touch of licorice-like spice.
Black tea and a nougat sweetness move forward over a creamy texture to the last inch.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Kintsugi Robusto blind review

alec-bradley--gatekeeper.description: Made in partnership with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo, Gatekeeper wraps Nicaraguan and Dominican filler and a Nicaraguan binder in an Ecuadorian Habano leaf. It begins with dry cocoa and a gentle pepper retrohale, turns earthier with baking spice and cedar, and ends on nutty, leathery tones; balanced and medium in body.

thirds.notes: Dry cocoa and a sweet-salty start, with white and red pepper on the retrohale.
Cocoa fades behind earth, baking spice and cedar as the strength edges up.
Chocolate-covered nuts, leather and cedar, with a touch of anise near the end.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Gatekeeper Toro blind review

alec-bradley--magic-toast.description: Named after a whiskey toast to a newly found tobacco crop, Magic Toast combines a Honduran wrapper with Nicaraguan and Honduran binder and filler. Medium to full, it starts malty with white pepper and a caramel sweetness, picks up citrus and baking spice through the middle and returns to a sweeter, earthy finish.

thirds.notes: Malty and slightly grainy at first, with white pepper on the retrohale and a caramel-like sweetness.
The body eases; pepper and citrus are joined by cinnamon and nutmeg over an earthy core.
The malt and gentle sweetness come back over the coffee-and-earth base as the strength rises slightly.

alec-bradley--project-40.description: Named after research suggesting that about forty percent of happiness comes from personal choices, Project 40 sets a Brazilian Habano binder between a Nicaraguan wrapper and Nicaraguan filler. Mild to medium in strength, it shows leather, nuts and caramel, with coffee, raisin, cream and baking spice; a relaxed, everyday cigar.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Project 40 06.52 blind review
Cigar Coop – Alec Bradley Project 40 06.52 review

thirds.notes: Coffee and raisin lead, with baking spice, a little cream and black pepper on the retrohale.
Coffee stays in charge; raisin comes and goes and a light black pepper shows on the tongue.
Earth joins coffee in front, while pepper, baking spice and raisin stay in the background.

alec-bradley--project-40-maduro.description: The darker counterpart to Project 40 within the Experimental Series, with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, Brazilian Habano binder and Nicaraguan filler. It opens malty with wood and earth, adds coffee and a smooth black pepper through the middle and fades to a soft spice over earth; medium-full and relaxed in pace.

thirds.notes: A malty start with wood and a rich, earthy depth.
The malt gives way to earthy coffee, a hint of salt and smooth black pepper on the retrohale.
The pepper fades into a gentle spice, leaving a quiet, earthy close.

alec-bradley--prensado-lost-art.description: A version of Prensado made by older methods: each cigar is bunched entubado for an open draw, lightly pressed and finished with a triple cap, around a Honduran wrapper with Honduran and Nicaraguan binder and filler. Hazelnut, white pepper and earth open, a floral note follows, and the finish turns creamy and earthy.

thirds.notes: Hazelnut, white pepper and earth in a full, aromatic opening.
The spice drops back on the palate, leaving a floral note while white pepper lingers on the retrohale.
Smooth and creamy, with earthy notes returning for the finish.

sources.title: Stogie Press – Prensado Lost Art review

alec-bradley--maxx.description: Conceived for large ring gauges, MAXX draws on tobacco from five countries: a Nicaraguan wrapper, a Costa Rican binder and filler from Colombia, Nicaragua, Mexico and Honduras. Medium in body, it is built on warm toast and baked-bread notes over a deep earthiness, with a soft natural sweetness from the binder.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – MAXX by Alec Bradley Toro blind review

thirds.notes: Chocolate, nuts and slightly burnt coffee, with cream and pepper on the retrohale.
Dark chocolate and semi-bitter espresso, turning sweeter and creamier as a peppery spice builds.
Sweet dark chocolate and espresso with nuts and pepper, and a slightly fuller body.

alec-bradley--american-classic.description: An easygoing blend with a Honduran Connecticut-seed wrapper over a Nicaraguan binder and filler. It starts light and smooth with coffee and cream, gathers a nutty, woody depth and a little spice, and ends somewhat fuller than it begins; a mild-to-medium cigar for any hour of the day.

thirds.notes: A dry, light start that settles into light coffee and cream.
Little change in direction; coffee and cream hold over a nutty, woody undertone.
Spice appears near the end and the strength steps up to medium.

sources.title: The Smoke Master Blog – American Classic review

alec-bradley--american-sun-grown.description: An all-Nicaraguan blend made entirely from sun-grown tobacco, wrapper, binder and filler alike. Medium in body and bolder than the American Classic, it offers a warm, understated sweetness, toasted nuts and a roasted coffee core with a clean finish; an everyday cigar with a little more edge.

sources.title: Crooked Burn – Alec Bradley American Sun Grown review
Cigar Reviews by the Katman – Alec Bradley American Sun Grown Blend

thirds.notes: A light, tingling spice and soft espresso, soon joined by leather, cocoa and a creamy edge.
Leather takes the lead with bitter baking chocolate; red pepper, raisin and light coffee add depth.
Leather and cocoa are at their fullest, with a long finish and a strength that keeps building.

alec-bradley--connecticut.description: A modern nod to the Connecticut shade cigar with which Alec Bradley began in the 1990s: a Connecticut wrapper over a Honduran binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Mild to medium, it keeps a clean cedar line throughout, with toasted nuts and a soft, baked toastiness; a calm morning or daytime smoke.

alec-bradley--lineage.description: Lineage combines a Honduran wrapper with a Nicaraguan binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler, offered in sizes up to a 70 ring gauge. Medium in body, it is grounded in earth with dry cedar, while the binder adds a light citrus lift that keeps the smoke fresh and balanced.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Alec Bradley Family Blend The Lineage Robusto quick review

thirds.notes: A creamy, woody opening with spice on the retrohale and a brief savoury, meaty note.
Spicy cedar takes over, then the wood turns towards oak as the creaminess grows.
A dry, cracker-like note and smooth retrohale spice, with cream and a faint mint to the end.

alec-bradley--tempus-natural.description: Built around an estate-grown tobacco from Trojes, Honduras, and named after the Latin word for time, Tempus pairs a Honduran wrapper with Honduran and Sumatran binders and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Medium to full, it moves from wood, pepper and cocoa to espresso and toasted nuts, ending with cedar and spice.

thirds.notes: Woody and peppery with a hint of cocoa and a mild, creamy finish.
Espresso and toasted nuts appear in a creamy smoke, with an earthy undertone.
Aromatic cedar and spice lead, cocoa and espresso linger, and the strength builds.

alec-bradley--medalist.description: Released in 2018 as a nod to the company's milder past, Medalist is rolled at Tabacos de Oriente in Honduras from a Honduran wrapper and binder with Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Mild to medium, it shows cedar and oak, a stone-fruit sweetness and baking spice over a smooth, creamy texture.

thirds.notes: Stone-fruit sweetness and baking spice over oak, with a floral retrohale.
A graham-cracker sweetness stays prominent as oak and a hint of pine grow.
Oak leads, the floral note fades and a mild, creamy sweetness rounds off the finish.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Medalist Robusto blind review

alec-bradley--texas-lancero.description: Despite its name, the Texas Lancero is a broad 7 x 70 cigar finished with a pigtail cap. A Nicaraguan wrapper and an Indonesian binder hold filler from Nicaragua, Honduras and Costa Rica. Medium in body, it opens bright with citrus, then shows smooth leather and toasted nuts on a balanced finish.

alec-bradley--occidental-reserve.description: Alec Bradley's longest-running brand, reworked in 2023, Occidental Reserve uses long filler from the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Nicaragua and Honduras under a Honduran Connecticut wrapper and a Nicaraguan binder. Mild to medium, it is creamy and nutty, with a gentle pepper that builds slowly on the finish; an easy daily cigar.

alec-bradley--filthy-hooligan.description: A yearly spring release in limited numbers, Filthy Hooligan spirals a green candela leaf and a dark Nicaraguan oscuro into a barber-pole wrapper, sharing Black Market's Sumatran binder and Honduran and Panamanian filler. Medium in body, it pairs lively spice and crisp pepper with a roasted, slightly bitter coffee core.

alec-bradley--tempus-nicaragua.description: A Nicaraguan counterpart to the Honduran Tempus, now discontinued, made entirely from Nicaraguan wrapper, binder and filler. Medium to full, it rests on a deep, mineral earthiness with a warm spice that develops steadily and a black pepper finish; a cigar to take time over.

alec-bradley--coyol.description: Named after the La Vega Coyol farm in Honduras and the coyol palm at its entrance, this discontinued line used a Honduran wrapper with Honduran and Nicaraguan binder and filler. Medium in body, it is earthy and leathery, with a measured spice from the Nicaraguan tobacco that builds gradually on the finish.

sources.title: Cigar Coop – Alec Bradley Coyol Toro review
Blind Man's Puff – Alec Bradley Coyol Robusto blind review

thirds.notes: Pepper is lively at first, then cedar, earth and leather take over, with some nuttiness behind.
Cedar and earth carry the middle; pepper builds again and a baking-spice note joins the leather.
Pepper and earth dominate the finish, with leather and a quieter cedar underneath.

alec-bradley--nica-puro.description: Alec Bradley's first Nicaraguan puro, now discontinued, was made to show the range of Nicaraguan tobacco across wrapper, binder and filler. Medium to full, it opens on a savoury leather base, carries a smooth cocoa sweetness through the middle and adds a light, nutmeg-like baking spice.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – Alec Bradley Nica Puro Churchill blind review

thirds.notes: Espresso and charred oak open the smoke, with black pepper, some chocolate and a meaty, molasses-like depth.
The oak softens as coffee and a mineral note grow; hints of cinnamon and licorice appear.
Black pepper comes to the front over espresso, dark chocolate and earth.

alec-bradley--post-embargo.description: Rolled at Raíces Cubanas in Honduras, the original Post Embargo, now discontinued, pairs a Honduran wrapper with Nicaraguan and Honduran binder and filler, aiming for old-world balance with new-world tobacco. Medium to full, it combines a savoury, earthy core, warming spice and a smooth cocoa note with light natural sweetness.
